name: BELARUS
lead: Belarus is a flat country in Eastern Europe. Ancient forests wrap around it, and lakes dot the land. Bison and lynx live in the woods. Belarusians love potatoes, folk embroidery, and ice hockey.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Belarus is almost perfectly flat. The whole country fits inside just 345 metres of height! Rivers like the Dnieper drift through the Palesse, a huge wetland.
About 40% of Belarus is pine and spruce forest. Over 10,000 glacial lakes (made by old ice) sparkle across the north. Belarus has no coast. It borders Poland, Ukraine, Russia, Latvia, and Lithuania.
animals: The European bison, or zubr, is the national animal. Hunters wiped it out in the wild by 1927. People bred it in zoos and set it free again. Białowieża Forest now has around 1,000 wild bison.
Białowieża also shelters wolves, lynx, and river otters. White storks nest on village chimneys. Locals think they bring luck. Thousands of cranes stop in the Pripyat marshes each autumn.
culture: Vyshyvanka is fine red-and-white embroidery on shirts and festival costumes. The potato (bulba) is a national favourite. Draniki, crispy potato pancakes, are on every table.
Ice hockey is the national sport. At Kupalle, a midsummer festival, young people leap over bonfires and float flower wreaths.
history: Between the 14th and 16th centuries, Belarus was the core of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. It was one of Europe's biggest states. It stretched from the Baltic almost to the Black Sea.
The Nazi occupation of 1941–44 was terrible. Belarus lost roughly a quarter of its people. It was rebuilt as a Soviet showcase republic. Independence came in 1991, when the USSR broke up.
wows: Białowieża Forest is Europe's last primeval lowland forest.
Minsk was rebuilt from scratch after WWII.
Belarus grows about 430 kg of potatoes per person each year.
Its highest 'peak', Dzyarzhynsk Hill, is just 345 m tall.
Belarus brought European bison back to the wild.
Vitebsk is the birthplace of Marc Chagall, whose dreamlike paintings hang worldwide.
Belarus helped found the UN in 1945, as part of the USSR.

myths.fact: True buffalo live in Africa and Asia. Bison are cousins in the cattle family.
That is an old story. Real white storks fly to Africa for the winter.
